items.item:
6. Two accepted changes in turn write entries numbered n and n + 1, and the
   audit sequence (M12) holds n + 1 after the second; two concurrent changes
   take two distinct consecutive numbers, and the one whose transaction
   committed first holds the lower.
   Shows A15-1. [witness: verification:registry_a15_sequential_and_concurrent_changes_number_in_order]
statements: for entries e1 written before e2: e1.sequence < e2.sequence   -- A15-1

verdicts.why: The check verifies sequential accepted changes receive n and n + 1 and that M12 advances accordingly; it also verifies concurrent changes receive distinct consecutive numbers. For the concurrent erasures, the removal counts identify which transaction applied first, and each possible ordering is explicitly checked to give that entry the lower sequence number.
